title: Evaluating the therapeutic role of salvianolic acid A on pancreatic cancer cells through interaction with the intrinsically disordered protein NUPR1.
authors: Alvarez-Rodriguez, Maria Gabriela; Estaras, Matias; Hornos, Felipe; Rizzuti, Bruno; Santofimia-Castano, Patricia; Iovanna, Juan L; Neira, Jose L
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物SAA靶向无序蛋白NUPR1的相互作用，虽含分子对接模拟，但对象为蛋白-小分子而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合建模关联较弱。
abstract: The nuclear protein 1 (NUPR1) is an intrinsically disordered protein (IDP) involved in stress processes in the cell. We have been developing, by using organic chemistry, several small molecules which hamper in vitro and in cell-based assays NUPR1 biomolecular interactions by targeting its two hot-spots around Ala33 and Thr68. In this work, we used a natural compound, salvianolic acid A (SAA), to target NUPR1. SAA has anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory properties. Binding in vitro was monitored by using fluorescence, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR); the affinity was in the low micromolar range, as shown by fluorescence and ITC. The NMR spectra of NUPR1, in the absence and in the presence of SAA, indicated that binding involved several polypeptide patches of NUPR1, as well as its hot-spots; however, the binding did not alter the disordered nature of the protein. Moreover, molecular docking simulations provided a model of the binding at the atomic level. Results of proliferation cellular assays with MIA PaCa-2 cells indicated that the IC(50) was ~20 muM, confirming the affinity values found by fluorescence and ITC. SAA was also capable of inhibiting the formation of stress granules (SGs) triggered by NUPR1. Our work shows that a plant-derived molecule can target an IDP involved in cancer, with affinities in the low micromolar range. Our model compound can hamper the pathological state (SG formation) triggered by this IDP, and indicates that the search for potential inhibitors of disordered proteins could be further extended to bioactive natural compounds.
abstract_zh: 核蛋白1（NUPR1）是一种 intrinsically disordered protein (IDP)，参与细胞内的应激过程。我们通过有机化学方法，开发了几种小分子，通过靶向其两个热点区域（Ala33和Thr68）来抑制NUPR1在体外和基于细胞的测定中的生物分子相互作用。在本工作中，我们使用了一种天然化合物——丹酚酸A（SAA）来靶向NUPR1。SAA具有抗癌和抗炎特性。体外结合通过荧光、等温滴定量热法（ITC）和核磁共振（NMR）进行监测；亲和力处于低微摩尔范围，如荧光和ITC所示。在不存在和存在SAA的情况下，NUPR1的NMR谱图表明，结合涉及NUPR1的多个多肽片段及其热点区域；然而，结合并未改变该蛋白的无序性质。此外，分子对接模拟提供了原子水平上的结合模型。使用MIA PaCa-2细胞进行的增殖细胞测定结果表明，IC(50)约为20 μM，证实了荧光和ITC测得的亲和力值。SAA还能抑制由NUPR1触发的应激颗粒（SGs）的形成。我们的工作表明，一种植物来源的分子可以靶向参与癌症的IDP，亲和力处于低微摩尔范围。我们的模型化合物能够抑制该IDP触发的病理状态（SG形成），并表明对无序蛋白潜在抑制剂的研究可进一步扩展至生物活性天然化合物。
